Somewhere, inside the Halls of Moonlight, a spectre, dressed in the white garbs of the Speaker, knocked on an otherwise unremarkable door.

"Well, do come in." Came the mind from inside.

The Speaker turned the knob, and eased the door open, and saw the peculiar sight that was Phaedrus's office. In particular, she looked with some disdain at the large shelf full of shoes, 48 pairs in all, arranged perfectly from the darkest blues to the palest reds. All of them were seeming placed perfectly in parallel.

Other peculiarities included an array of flat, silvery disks that were littered on his desk, some of which had small filaments of silver wire on them, another of his rather bizarre experiments presumably. Many vases were also present, seemingly evenly spaced around the room, all of which were empty for the time being. An odd sight, seeing as Phaedrus often confessed that he was not particularly interested in the field of botany.

"So, shall we begin?" Phaedrus remained seated, dragging a chair across the room with a small twitch of his hand. "I think we both know why you are here."

The Speaker sat down suspiciously, *"What exactly do you think I'm here for?"*

"You are here because you have problems, and you require solutions. I only wished you shared my concern at the inexplicable phenomenon that has recently struck our research division. Papers have often gotten filed, sometimes while unfinished, always while nobody is present. It is peculiar, to have poltergeists fiddling with our lives."

As if on cue, a single, slightly slanted shoe shifted, and Phaedrus sighed.

"No, you are here because we have a particular Lethe problem in Kureta. Casualties have been rather light, and several lethe have been detected and exterminated, as unfortunate as such an event is. However, you don't want this hasty intervention do you? No, you need a methodical approach, a solution to our problems, preferably a permanent one."

The Speaker nodded, this was indeed the issue she had come to raise. *"So you have not been unaware? I was under the impression that you had been holed up in your study since your return. I can only wonder about the source of your information."*

"Oh yes, I have been, but rumors have a tendency to spread. I have my sources, they are irrelevant. Unfortunately, as I see it, there is no real solution to the Lethe problem. the construction of additional fortification is necessary, as is the continued devotion of Order of Force solders to Kureta. Use of Order of Flux assassins to help bait and disorientate the Lethe, followed by selected target assassinations is also continuing. I can only advise further vigilance. As for weaponry, I'm afraid there are certain problems with current designs."

Phaedrus picked up a wooden top, another one of his odd habits, collecting items of little apparent value, yet Phaedrus was as brilliant as he was incomprehensible. He spun it with one hand and stared at it admiringly.

*"What is the meaning of this nonsense, are you saying you can offer no assistance?"*

"Not immediately, research into weaponry has been low priority, although magical implements have had significant progress. Floatstone optimization has been refined to a science, and is readily reproducable now. In addition, recent experiments have been made into making these "circuits" so to speak. These wafers are woefully incomplete, I asked Quadrivus for a favour concerning this particular development though. Basically, we've found some basic configurations lead to particular effects. For example, this particular array causes rapid heating of the element, resulting in melting, while this one has caused the air above it to glow, and specifically the air above it."

*"And?"* The Speaker was getting impatient, this was a massive waste of time.

"I believe with time and resources, this could be weaponized, we can prioritize this right away, but Iskandir has to get back to his forge."

*"So we wait on Quadrivus?"*

"For this purpose, yes. However, there is a more pressing matter we have to address. Surely you have noticed all the tiny changes that occur when you aren't looking? Remember when there was always that one spec of dust that your cleaner never got on your desk? When was the last time you saw that spot? Have you noticed how all your pens are perfectly arranged, while your cleaner left them a jumbled mess before? Well I have, and it worries me, it should also worry you."

*"Why? Doesn't this lead to increased productivity, I find it to be a nice change, if the things you said were true."*

"Two reasons, compromise of important state secrets, and it has led to decreased productivity. Some of my reports have been filed while they were mostly finished, but lacking some finishing touches. There have been some impacts to worker efficiency, and documentation errors are creeping in, only a few, yet a few makes a huge difference. The Order of Moonlight is dependent on this documentation to function."

*"And your proposal?"*

"Well, it sounds crazy," Phaedrus lifted a pen and placed it slightly off parallel to the edge of his desk. "If you would, please examine that painting for just a second."

As the Speaker turned, Phaedrus opened a cabinet, withdrew a flower, and with a clang, a pen that was lifting into the air fell to the table.

The Speaker jumped, and fired a bolt of light at Phaedrus, only to have it absorbed harmlessly.

"This particular flower seems to rid our unwelcome guests of their influence. I need your permission to spread these throughout the Orders. Surely you understand, we have many secrets, and they must be protected."

The Speaker looked at the Orchid, surely Phaedrus was joking! A flower to repel Poltergeists, a superstition no doubt.

"I assure you, I am not joking. Please consider, and take this flower as a gift, it matches your cloak anyways." Phaedrus tossed the vase into the air.

With utter confusion, the Speaker caught it effortlessly, and with a sense of complete bemusement and annoyance, stormed out of the room.

Smirking, Phaedrus took out a lab page titled "shoe movement" and placed the four-hundred-seventy-eighth tick mark onto the page, and recorded the number with the shoe colour, mass of shoe, and its position on the shelf, as well as many other pieces of presumably relevant information.

It was going to be a long bit of work ahead of him, and there were concerns he simply did not share.

Tales of Daemons, a bane upon the Schrykes, have been spreading. These projects had to go quicker than he would like to ensure the survival of the Spectra as a people.

Quadrivus better finish his request soon, for all their sakes.
